title: Car Seat Guide: Stages, Rules and Fitting Tips
description: Car seats by stage, from rear-facing infant seats to boosters: the law in the UK, US and Europe, i-Size R129, fitting checks and the coat rule.
intro: A correctly fitted car seat is one of the most important things you will buy. Here are the stages, the rules and the checks that matter.

image.alt: A grey and black child car seat in a car

sections.h2: Rules in the UK, Europe and the US
sections.html:
WhereMain rules
UKChildren must use a child car seat until they are 12 years old or 135cm tall, whichever comes first. Only EU-approved seats (R44 or R129) can be used. Never fit a rear-facing seat in front of an active airbag. Under R129 (i-Size), babies stay rear-facing until at least 15 months.
EUEU law requires children under 150cm to use an approved child restraint (some countries set 135cm). New seats are approved to UN R129 (i-Size).
USLaws vary by state. The AAP advises rear-facing for as long as possible, until the highest height or weight the seat allows, then a forward-facing harness, then a belt-positioning booster until the seat belt fits (usually at about 4 ft 9 in / 145cm, between ages 8 and 12). Children under 13 should ride in the back seat. Seats must meet FMVSS 213.

• Tight install: the seat should move no more than about an inch (2.5cm) side to side at the belt path or ISOFIX base.
  • Harness: snug enough that you can't pinch any slack at the shoulder (the “pinch test”). Chest clip at armpit level (US seats).
  • No bulky coats: take off puffy coats and snowsuits before buckling; tuck a blanket over the harness instead.
  • Recline: newborns need the correct recline angle so their head doesn't flop forward.
  • Not for sleep at home: move your baby to a flat sleep space after the journey. Many manufacturers also advise regular breaks on long trips.

sections.h2: Second-hand seats and getting a check
sections.html: Avoid second-hand car seats unless you know their full history: a seat that has been in a crash may be damaged in ways you can't see, and seats have expiry dates in the US. Free fitting help: in the US, a certified Child Passenger Safety Technician via NHTSA; in the UK, many retailers offer fitting checks, and childcarseats.org.uk (RoSPA) explains the rules.

faqs.q: When can my baby face forward in the car?
faqs.a: Keep your child rear-facing for as long as their seat allows. In the UK and EU, R129 (i-Size) seats require rear-facing until at least 15 months. The AAP advises staying rear-facing until your child reaches the seat’s rear-facing height or weight limit, which for many seats is age 2 or older.

faqs.q: When can a child stop using a booster seat in the UK?
faqs.a: UK law says children must use a child car seat until they are 12 years old or 135cm tall, whichever comes first. Many safety experts recommend using a booster until 150cm.

faqs.q: Can my baby wear a coat in a car seat?
faqs.a: Take off thick or puffy coats and snowsuits before buckling, because they can stop the harness fitting tightly. Use thin layers and put a blanket or coat over the top of the harness instead.
